scope: Independent read-only review of target executor implementation; no production source edits, no child agents, no hardware execution.
result: No remaining concrete blocker found in the final source hashes and audited ELF files. This is source/native/build review, not physical or vehicle qualification.

findings.finding: A newer command consumed before an already queued crank edge caused AngleScheduler::tooth to reject the older capture timestamp and Executor::commit to latch an invalid-angle-plan fault during normal command/capture interleaving.
findings.initial_repro: queued-command-probe.cpp: capture 1000 us, command 1010 us, commit 1012 us => valid=0, Commit::Fault, invalid_angle_plan. Compiled with -O2 -fsanitize=address,undefined against initial-source hashes.
findings.fix_review: Worker still decodes each current capture, counts captures older than latest command/sample as superseded, and schedules only eligible captures. The independent 1000 us capture-age rejection remains active.

findings.finding: One-shot epoch invalidation around sensor-profile persistence allowed the application to tag a cached old profile with the new epoch and reactivate while persistence was still underway.
findings.repro: Interleaving: invalidate epoch; application retains old Config; submit old-profile command with new epoch before config_put publishes the changed profile.
findings.fix_review: Configuration hold spans persistence and active publication, rejects submits and queued commands, increments epoch on release, and enforces tune/sensor revision floors. Captures are epoch-tagged, held/old captures are ignored, and the decoder resets on epoch change.

findings.finding: A latched OutputIO Gate failure could be periodically cleared by Executor recovery and re-tripped on the next supervision iteration, briefly reporting timing_fault=false despite a reset-only physical failure. An unready initial capture clock could similarly lose its timing fault.
findings.fix_review: Recovery now requires capture_clock.ready(), !output.failed, no configuration hold, and matching accepted/current epochs in addition to fresh stopped/quiet inputs.

findings.finding: The dummy-load environment claimed to omit radio service, but ECU_COMPACT_A3 still selected the full ESP-NOW/Wi-Fi/pairing task and its uncoordinated NVS writes.
findings.fix_review: Dummy-load builds select no-op radio functions. Audited dummy ELF has a 5-byte radio::start no-op and no radio task implementation.

findings.finding: Decoder-loss shutdown reused time sampled before decoding outside the target lock. An intervening compare ISR could make cut actual_us precede the just-recorded rise and report a zero high width.
findings.fix_review: The shutdown now samples now_locked() after taking the target lock.

findings.finding: IRAM_ATTR on outlined class/COMDAT methods produced Xtensa dangerous l32r literal-pool relocations, preventing the selected target link.
findings.fix_review: Header ISR helpers are forced inline into explicitly IRAM callback roots; both final ELF files pass the call/literal/data audit below.

validation.native: firmware/tests/timing_executor_test.cpp compiled with c++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -I firmware/include and passed. See final-native-tests.log.
validation.target_builds: Parent build log .cache/engine/target-build-final.log reports compact_n16r8_web and compact_a3_timing_bench successful; this reviewer independently inspected their actual final ELF files.
validation.elf_audit_method: audit_elf.py recursively follows direct calls from both application callbacks and both IDF driver ISR roots, checks literal locations/loaded flash pointers, and resolves application callx targets to ROM. It follows actual branch/fall-through PCs and re-decodes incomplete instructions because GNU linear Xtensa disassembly can misdecode jump-over padding. Driver callback indirections were manually matched to source registrations.

virtual-final.callback_indirections_review: The two unresolved indirect calls are the IDF driver invocations of the registered on_capture/on_alarm callbacks, which point to the audited IRAM roots.

dummy-final.callback_indirections_review: The two unresolved indirect calls are the IDF driver invocations of the registered on_capture/on_alarm callbacks, which point to the audited IRAM roots.

validation.queue_storage: Pinned IDF FreeRTOS pvPortMalloc uses MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT. Queues are created with xQueueCreate and target ISR objects are in internal DRAM.

limits: No physical hardware, engine or vehicle qualification was performed.
actual_us/max_lateness/high-duration software counters use one dispatch timestamp for sequential writes; these are not per-pin electrical edge measurements.
Interrupt latency and ISR duration, cache-disabled behavior on hardware, capture-latch overwrite/lost-edge behavior, electrical gate response and physical pulse width/jitter remain unmeasured.
